decisions.reason: A product line with several models that has its own page shows substantial investment and visible commitment, so management would persist rather than write it off after only one year.

Floor-level shower drainage is central to the firm's announced direction toward low-profile, accessible systems, so dropping it would contradict that strategy even though it is only mentioned on the website.
As the presented flagship of the firm's direction, it carries strong public commitment and investment, and abandoning it would expose the strategic choice as a mistake.
The integrated-slope shower element fits the integrated floor-level direction, and with little time on the market any weak results can still be attributed to temporary ramp-up causes.
The firm announced this backflow drain publicly as its own development, with a dedicated page, so the commitment and sunk development costs favour persistence.

The air-admittance valve is peripheral, only mentioned, and carries little public commitment, which makes it the likeliest drop candidate, but one year is too short to rule out temporary causes for weak results.
